# Command reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-command-docs.zsh. Run `make docs` after changing flags. -->

The canonical help for any command is `zui help <command>`. This page mirrors the
live option definitions. Types are `flag`, `str`, `int` or `multi` (repeatable).

## Global options

These may precede the command:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | Show help (use `zui help <cmd>` for one command). |
| `-v, --version` | Print the version. |
| `--theme NAME` | Palette: default, light, dracula, gruvbox, nord, solarized, catppuccin, mono. |
| `--no-color` | Disable colour (also honours `NO_COLOR`). |
| `--ascii` | ASCII borders and glyphs. |
| `--debug` | Debug output on stderr. |

## Exit codes

`0` success · `1` cancel/negative · `2` usage error · `3` no terminal · `124` timeout · `130` Ctrl-C.

## `choose`

Pick one item, or many with --no-limit/--limit.

```text
zui choose [flags] [items...]
```

A scrollable selection window. Type to filter, use arrows to move, Space to mark items when multiple selection is enabled, and Enter to confirm. Items come from arguments or from stdin, one per line.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-l`, `--limit` | int | 1 | Maximum number of items to select |
| `--no-limit` | flag | — | Allow any number of selections |
| `-o`, `--ordered` | flag | — | Return selections in the order they were chosen |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Number of visible list rows (0 = fit content) |
| `--header` | str | Choose | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--cursor` | str | >  | Prefix drawn before the focused row |
| `--selected` | multi | — | Item selected when the dialog opens (repeatable) |
| `--select-if-one` | flag | — | Return immediately when only one item exists |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration (e.g. 10s) |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--no-fuzzy` | flag | — | Use substring matching instead of fuzzy matching |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `↑/↓, k/j` | Move the cursor |
| `PgUp/PgDn` | Jump one screen |
| `Space` | Toggle the focused item (multi-select) |
| `Enter` | Confirm the selection |
| `Tab` | Move focus to the buttons |
| `/` | Focus the filter line |
| `Esc` | Clear the filter, or cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Clear the filter, or cancel'
printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma' | zui choose --header "Pick one"
zui choose --no-limit --header "Packages" curl git zsh
zui choose --limit 3 --ordered --selected git < packages.txt
zui choose --select-if-one --header "Version" < versions.txt
```

**Notes**

line='zui choose --select-if-one --header "Version" < versions.txt'
- With --limit greater than 1, Space marks items and Enter confirms. Without a mark, Enter accepts the focused item.
- Esc returns 1, Ctrl-C returns 130, and --timeout returns 124.

## `confirm`

Ask a yes/no question with two focused buttons.

```text
zui confirm [flags] [question]
```

A two-button confirmation dialog. Enter triggers the default answer, arrows or Tab move between buttons, and Esc cancels. By default nothing is printed: use the exit status (0 yes, 1 no, 130 aborted, 124 timeout).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--affirmative` | str | Yes | Label for the yes button |
| `--negative` | str | No | Label for the no button |
| `--default` | str | yes | Default answer: yes or no |
| `--show-output` | flag | — | Print true or false |
| `--message` | str | — | Question text (arguments are used when omitted) |
| `--header` | str | Confirm | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='Esc returns 1, Ctrl-C returns 130, and --timeout returns 124.'
| `←/→` | Move between the buttons |
| `Enter` | Choose the focused button |
| `Tab` | Cycle focus |
| `Esc` | Cancel (exit 1) |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel (exit 1)'
zui confirm "Deploy to production?" && ./deploy.sh
zui confirm --default no --affirmative Discard --negative Keep "Discard 3 files?"
zui confirm --show-output "Enable telemetry?"
```

**Notes**

line='zui confirm --show-output "Enable telemetry?"'
- --show-output prints true for Yes and false for No. Esc and Ctrl-C print nothing.

## `input`

Read a single line of text in a framed input dialog.

```text
zui input [flags]
```

A single-line editor with a block caret, horizontal scrolling, Home/End, word movement and optional password masking. Enter confirms, Esc cancels.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--value` | str | — | Initial value |
| `--placeholder` | str | — | Hint shown while the field is empty |
| `--prompt` | str | — | Short prefix drawn before the field |
| `--password` | flag | — | Mask the value with bullets |
| `--char-limit` | int | 0 | Maximum number of characters (0 = unlimited) |
| `--header` | str | Input | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='--show-output prints true for Yes and false for No. Esc and Ctrl-C print nothing.'
| `←/→` | Move the caret |
| `Home/End` | Jump to the start or end |
| `Ctrl-A/Ctrl-E` | Start or end |
| `Ctrl-U/Ctrl-K` | Delete before or after the caret |
| `Ctrl-W, Alt-B/F` | Delete or move by word |
| `Enter` | Confirm |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
name=$(zui input --header "Your name" --placeholder "Ada Lovelace")
zui input --password --header "Password"
zui input --value main --prompt "branch:" --header "New branch"
```

**Notes**

line='zui input --value main --prompt "branch:" --header "New branch"'
- The value is printed on stdout after the UI is restored, so it is safe to capture with $(...).

## `write`

Compose multi-line text in a scrollable text area.

```text
zui write [flags]
```

A multi-line editor with wrapping-free horizontal scrolling, line numbers and an optional character limit. Ctrl-D or the Done button submits, Esc cancels.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--value` | str | — | Initial text (use \\n for newlines) |
| `--placeholder` | str | — | Hint shown while the buffer is empty |
| `--header` | str | Write | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--char-limit` | int | 0 | Maximum number of characters (0 = unlimited) |
| `--show-line-numbers` | flag | — | Show a line-number gutter |
| `--height` | int | 8 | Text area height in rows |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='The value is printed on stdout after the UI is restored, so it is safe to capture with $(...).'
| `Arrows` | Move the caret |
| `Home/End` | Start or end of line |
| `Enter` | New line |
| `Tab` | Insert two spaces |
| `Backspace/Delete` | Delete characters |
| `Ctrl-D` | Submit |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
body=$(zui write --header "Commit message" --show-line-numbers)
zui write --placeholder "Type notes..." --height 12 > notes.txt
```

**Notes**

line='zui write --placeholder "Type notes..." --height 12 > notes.txt'
- For scripted newlines in --value use a literal $\n in zsh: --value "one\ntwo".
- The final text is printed after the terminal is restored.

## `filter`

Fuzzy-filter a list and pick one line.

```text
zui filter [flags] [items...]
```

Like choose, but the filter line is always visible and the list is re-ranked as you type. Useful for short commands, branches, hosts and files.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--height` | int | 0 | Number of visible rows (0 = fit content) |
| `--header` | str | Filter | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--placeholder` | str | — | Hint for the filter line |
| `--value` | str | — | Initial filter text |
| `--no-fuzzy` | flag | — | Use substring matching instead of fuzzy matching |
| `--select-if-one` | flag | — | Return immediately when a single item remains |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='The final text is printed after the terminal is restored.'
| `type` | Narrow the list |
| `↑/↓` | Move the cursor |
| `Enter` | Return the focused item |
| `Esc` | Clear the filter, or cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Clear the filter, or cancel'
git branch --format="%(refname:short)" | zui filter --header "Checkout branch"
printf 'staging\nproduction\ndev' | zui filter --select-if-one
```

**Notes**

line='printf '\''staging\nproduction\ndev'\'' | zui filter --select-if-one'
- Matching is fuzzy by default: characters only need to appear in order. With --no-fuzzy, a case-insensitive substring must match.

## `file`

Browse directories and pick a file or directory.

```text
zui file [flags] [start]
```

A directory browser. Enter opens directories and selects files; Right opens a directory and Left goes to the parent. With --directory, Enter selects the highlighted directory (use Right to descend). Hidden entries are skipped unless --all/--show-hidden is given.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--cursor` | str | . | Starting directory or file |
| `--all` | flag | — | Show hidden entries |
| `--show-hidden` | flag | — | Show hidden entries |
| `--file` | flag | — | Allow files to be selected |
| `--directory` | flag | — | Allow directories to be selected |
| `--height` | int | 12 | Number of visible rows (0 = fit content) |
| `--header` | str | File | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='Matching is fuzzy by default: characters only need to appear in order. With --no-fuzzy, a case-insensitive substring must match.'
| `↑/↓` | Move the cursor |
| `Enter` | Open a directory or select an entry |
| `Right` | Open the highlighted directory |
| `Left` | Go to the parent directory |
| `type` | Filter entries |
| `Tab` | Focus the buttons |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
file=$(zui file --header "Open project")
dir=$(zui file --directory --header "Choose an output directory")
zui file --all --cursor ~/Projects
```

**Notes**

line='zui file --all --cursor ~/Projects'
- The selected path is always printed as an absolute path, even when you started from a relative directory.
- By default only files are selectable; --directory makes directories selectable too.

## `pager`

Scroll through text or a file in a framed window.

```text
zui pager [flags] [file]
```

Reads a file, or stdin when no file is given. When stdout is not a terminal the content is printed unchanged; otherwise it is shown in a scrollable window. No text is written to stdout in interactive mode.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--line-numbers` | flag | — | Show line numbers |
| `--header` | str | — | Title shown in the dialog title bar |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Window height in rows (0 = fit the terminal) |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='By default only files are selectable; --directory makes directories selectable too.'
| `↑/↓` | Scroll one line |
| `PgUp/PgDn` | Scroll five lines |
| `Home/End` | Jump to the top or bottom |
| `q/Esc/Enter` | Close |

**Examples**

```sh
line='q/Esc/Enter|Close'
zui pager README.md
kubectl describe pod my-pod | zui pager --line-numbers
zui pager --header "diff" < change.patch
```

**Notes**

line='zui pager --header "diff" < change.patch'
- Piping through zui pager is a no-op for non-interactive output, so it is safe in scripts.
- The pager exits 0 when closed and 124 on timeout.

## `spin`

Show a spinner while a command runs.

```text
zui spin [flags] -- command [args...]
```

Runs a command in the background while drawing a framed spinner, then forwards the requested output. The command's exit status becomes zui's exit status. Esc or Ctrl-C stops the command and returns 130.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--spinner` | str | dot | Spinner style: dot, line, minidot, jump, pulse, meter, ellipsis |
| `--title` | str | Working... | Label shown next to the spinner |
| `--align` | str | left | Label alignment: left, center, right |
| `--interval` | int | 80 | Frame interval in milliseconds |
| `--show-output` | flag | — | Print the command stdout when it finishes |
| `--show-error` | flag | — | Print the command stderr when it finishes |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='The pager exits 0 when closed and 124 on timeout.'
| `Esc` | Cancel the command (exit 130) |
| `Ctrl-C` | Cancel the command (exit 130) |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Ctrl-C|Cancel the command (exit 130)'
zui spin --title "Fetching..." -- git fetch --all
zui spin --spinner pulse --show-error -- make -j8
zui spin -- sleep 3 --show-output
```

**Notes**

line='zui spin -- sleep 3 --show-output'
- The child command receives /dev/null as stdin so it cannot steal keystrokes.
- When stdout is not a terminal the command runs directly and its output is not suppressed.

## `style`

Wrap text in borders, padding, margins and ANSI colour.

```text
zui style [flags] [text...]
```

A non-interactive styling primitive, useful for composing banners and status blocks. Colour accepts names (red, cyan, default), 256-colour indices (0-255) and hex values when the terminal supports truecolour.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--foreground` | str | — | Text colour: name, 0-255 or #rrggbb |
| `--background` | str | — | Background colour: name, 0-255 or #rrggbb |
| `--border` | str | rounded | Border: rounded, normal, thick, double, block, hidden, none |
| `--border-foreground` | str | — | Border foreground colour |
| `--border-background` | str | — | Border background colour |
| `--padding` | str | 0 | Inner padding: N or V,H or T,R,B,L |
| `--padding-background` | str | — | Padding background colour |
| `--margin` | str | 0 | Outer margin: N or V,H or T,R,B,L |
| `--margin-background` | str | — | Margin background colour |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Content width in columns (0 = fit text) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Content height in rows (0 = fit text) |
| `--align` | str | left | Horizontal alignment: left, center, right |
| `--bold` | flag | — | Bold text |
| `--italic` | flag | — | Italic text |
| `--underline` | flag | — | Underlined text |
| `--strikethrough` | flag | — | Struck-through text |
| `--faint` | flag | — | Faint text |
| `--text` | str | — | Text to style (also accepted as arguments) |

**Examples**

```sh
line='When stdout is not a terminal the command runs directly and its output is not suppressed.'
zui style --border rounded --padding 1,2 --foreground 212 "Hello"
zui style --border double --border-foreground 81 --bold "RELEASE 2.0"
zui style --background 236 --foreground 252 --padding 1,3 "quoted text"
zui style --margin 1 --margin-background 234 --align center "centred"
```

**Notes**

line='zui style --margin 1 --margin-background 234 --align center "centred"'
- Padding and margin accept one value (all sides), two values (vertical,horizontal) or four values (top,right,bottom,left).
- When stdout is not a terminal, ANSI escapes are omitted.

## `format`

Substitute {{.Fields}} in a template.

```text
zui format [flags] [key=value...]
```

A tiny, dependency-free template renderer for shell scripts.  Fields use Go-template spelling: {{.Name}} or {{ .Name }}.  Values are passed as key=value arguments, so no quoting surprises are introduced.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--template` | str | — | Template containing {{.Fields}} |
| `--file` | str | — | Read the template from a file |
| `--strict` | flag | — | Fail when a placeholder is left unresolved |

**Examples**

```sh
line='When stdout is not a terminal, ANSI escapes are omitted.'
zui format --template "Hello, {{.Name}}!" Name=Ada
printf '{{.Project}} v{{.Version}}' > tmpl; zui format --file tmpl Project=zui Version=0.1.0
zui format --strict --template "{{.A}}{{.B}}" A=1
```

**Notes**

line='zui format --strict --template "{{.A}}{{.B}}" A=1'
- With --strict, any {{...}} placeholder that remains after substitution is an error (exit 2).
- When no template is given, stdin is used.

## `join`

Join blocks of text horizontally or vertically.

```text
zui join [flags] [blocks...]
```

Blocks come from arguments, or from stdin split on lines containing only ---. Horizontal joins place blocks side by side, padding shorter blocks; vertical stacks them, padding narrower blocks.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--direction` | str | horizontal | Join direction: horizontal or vertical |
| `--align` | str | left | Block alignment: left, center, right |
| `--padding` | int | 1 | Spaces (horizontal) or blank lines (vertical) between blocks |
| `--horizontal` | flag | — | Shorthand for --direction horizontal |
| `--vertical` | flag | — | Shorthand for --direction vertical |

**Examples**

```sh
line='When no template is given, stdin is used.'
printf 'one\ntwo\n---\nA\nB\nC' | zui join --horizontal
zui join --vertical --align center --padding 2 "left block" "a longer block"
printf 'x\n---\ny' | zui join --direction vertical
```

**Notes**

line='printf '\''x\n---\ny'\'' | zui join --direction vertical'
- Alignment applies to each line inside its block.
- Horizontal joins trim trailing spaces from each output line.

## `table`

Render CSV data as an aligned, bordered table.

```text
zui table [flags]
```

Parses CSV (including quoted fields and escaped quotes) and prints a boxed table. The first row is used as the header unless --columns or --no-header is supplied. Column widths are computed from the content and clamped to the terminal width.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--columns` | str | — | Comma-separated header names (otherwise the first row is the header) |
| `--widths` | str | — | Comma-separated column widths |
| `--separator` | str | , | Field separator |
| `--file` | str | — | Read CSV from a file instead of stdin |
| `--border` | str | rounded | Border: rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |
| `--print` | flag | — | Print the table (default behaviour) |
| `--no-header` | flag | — | Treat every row as data |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Accepted for gum compatibility (tables are static) |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Horizontal joins trim trailing spaces from each output line.'
printf 'name,age\nAda,36\nGrace,45' | zui table
zui table --file users.csv --columns "Name,Role" --widths 20,30
zui table --separator "\t" --file metrics.tsv
```

**Notes**

line='zui table --separator "\t" --file metrics.tsv'
- This implementation renders a static table, which makes it safe in pipelines. Use --print explicitly if you prefer.
- Widths count characters; wide CJK glyphs may shift alignment.

## `log`

Emit a levelled, optionally structured log line.

```text
zui log [flags] [message] [key=value...]
```

A small logger with coloured text output, logfmt and JSON. Positional key=value pairs become structured fields. Colours are disabled when writing to a file or when stdout is not a terminal.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--level` | str | info | Message level: debug, info, warn, error, fatal |
| `--min-level` | str | debug | Suppress messages below this level |
| `--prefix` | str | — | Prefix placed before the level |
| `--time` | str | — | Timestamp format (strftime) or rfc3339 |
| `--file` | str | — | Append the log line to a file instead of stdout |
| `--format` | str | text | Output format: text, logfmt or json |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Widths count characters; wide CJK glyphs may shift alignment.'
zui log --level info "server started" port=8080 env=dev
zui log --level error --format json "request failed" status=500 path=/api
zui log --time "%H:%M:%S" --prefix deploy "built image"
zui log --file app.log --level warn "disk low" free=2%
```

**Notes**

line='zui log --file app.log --level warn "disk low" free=2%'
- Levels are ordered debug < info < warn < error < fatal. --min-level filters messages below the threshold.
- JSON strings are escaped; logfmt values containing spaces are quoted.

## `dialog`

Open any dialog type from one flag-driven command.

```text
zui dialog --type TYPE [flags] [items...]
```

A programmatic front end for msgbox, yesno, inputbox, menu, checklist, form, gauge and infobox. Each type is forwarded to its dedicated command, so the flags and outputs are identical. Use the dedicated commands for discoverable per-type help.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--type` | str | msgbox | Dialog type: msgbox, yesno, inputbox, menu, checklist, form, gauge, infobox |
| `--title` | str | — | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Body text or question |
| `--icon` | str | info | Icon: info, success, warn, error, question |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form; repeat for more buttons (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |
| `--value` | str | — | Initial value for inputbox |
| `--placeholder` | str | — | Placeholder for inputbox |
| `--prompt` | str | — | Prompt prefix for inputbox |
| `--password` | flag | — | Mask the inputbox value |
| `--char-limit` | int | 0 | Inputbox character limit (0 = unlimited) |
| `--selected` | multi | — | Initially selected item(s) or menu cursor (repeatable) |
| `--limit` | int | 0 | Checklist selection limit (0 = unlimited) |
| `--no-limit` | flag | — | Allow unlimited checklist selections |
| `--ordered` | flag | — | Return checklist items in selection order |
| `--field` | multi | — | Form field in Label=value form (repeatable) |
| `--secret` | multi | — | Form field label to mask (repeatable) |
| `--percent` | int | 0 | Gauge percentage |
| `--label` | str | — | Gauge label under the bar |
| `--affirmative` | str | Yes | Yes button label for yesno |
| `--negative` | str | No | No button label for yesno |
| `--default-answer` | str | yes | Default answer for yesno: yes or no |
| `--show-output` | flag | — | Print true/false for yesno |
| `--print` | flag | — | Print a gauge instead of opening a dialog |

**Examples**

```sh
line='JSON strings are escaped; logfmt values containing spaces are quoted.'
zui dialog --type msgbox --message "Saved."
zui dialog --type yesno --message "Ship it?" --show-output
zui dialog --type inputbox --title "Name" --message "Your name:"
zui dialog --type checklist --selected docs "ui docs tests"
zui dialog --type form --field "Name=" --field "Email="
zui dialog --type gauge --percent 60 --label "Uploading"
```

**Notes**

line='zui dialog --type gauge --percent 60 --label "Uploading"'
- Types are validated before dispatch. Unknown types exit 2.
- Run zui help <type> for the complete option list of a dialog.

## `msgbox`

Show a message box with any number of action buttons.

```text
zui msgbox [flags] [message]
```

The core dialog(1)-style window: a framed message, an icon, and a row of buttons. Buttons are Label=action pairs and can run shell commands, print a value, or exit with a chosen status. Without --button, a single OK button is shown.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Message | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Body text (arguments are used when omitted) |
| `--icon` | str | info | Icon: info, success, warn, error, question |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form; repeat for more buttons (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button focused and triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='Run zui help <type> for the complete option list of a dialog.'
| `←/→, Tab` | Move between buttons |
| `Enter` | Run the focused button |
| `Alt-<letter>` | Run an &accelerator button |
| `Esc` | Cancel (exit 1) |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel (exit 1)'
zui msgbox "Build finished."
zui msgbox --icon warn --message "Disk almost full." --button "OK=exit:0" --button "Details=run:df -h"
zui msgbox --title "Update" --button "Later=exit:1" --button "Install=run:brew upgrade" "Install updates now?"
zui msgbox --timeout 5s "This closes on its own."
```

**Notes**

line='zui msgbox --timeout 5s "This closes on its own."'
- Any number of buttons is allowed; they wrap onto additional rows when needed.
- Actions: exit:N, accept, cancel, print:TEXT, run:COMMAND (run executes after the terminal is restored).

## `yesno`

A modal yes/no dialog with named affirmative and negative buttons.

```text
zui yesno [flags] [question]
```

The dialog(1) flavour of confirm: a framed question with two buttons. Exit status is 0 for yes, 1 for no, 130 for abort and 124 for timeout.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Question | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Question text (arguments are used when omitted) |
| `--affirmative` | str | Yes | Label for the yes button |
| `--negative` | str | No | Label for the no button |
| `--default-answer` | str | yes | Default answer: yes or no |
| `--show-output` | flag | — | Print true or false |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='Actions: exit:N, accept, cancel, print:TEXT, run:COMMAND (run executes after the terminal is restored).'
| `←/→` | Move between buttons |
| `Enter` | Choose the focused button |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
zui yesno "Restart the service?"
zui yesno --affirmative Overwrite --negative Skip --default-answer no "Overwrite config?"
zui yesno --show-output "Continue?"
```

**Notes**

line='zui yesno --show-output "Continue?"'
- --show-output prints true or false. Esc prints nothing and exits 1.

## `inputbox`

A framed text-input dialog with buttons.

```text
zui inputbox [flags]
```

Combines a message and a single-line editor in one dialog. By default the OK button accepts the value and prints it; custom buttons can print something else or run a command.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Input | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Label or prompt above the field |
| `--value` | str | — | Initial value |
| `--placeholder` | str | — | Hint shown while the field is empty |
| `--prompt` | str | — | Short prefix inside the field row |
| `--password` | flag | — | Mask the value |
| `--char-limit` | int | 0 | Maximum characters (0 = unlimited) |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form; repeat for more buttons (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='--show-output prints true or false. Esc prints nothing and exits 1.'
| `←/→` | Move the caret |
| `Home/End` | Start or end |
| `Enter` | Accept the value |
| `Tab` | Focus the buttons |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
zui inputbox --title "Rename" --message "New name:" --value old.txt
zui inputbox --password --title "Unlock" --message "Passphrase:"
zui inputbox --button "Save=accept" --button "Clear=print:" --button "Cancel=cancel" "Value:"
```

**Notes**

line='zui inputbox --button "Save=accept" --button "Clear=print:" --button "Cancel=cancel" "Value:"'
- The accepted value is printed to stdout after the UI closes.
- A custom button using print: emits its own value instead.

## `menu`

Pick one item from a list inside a dialog with buttons.

```text
zui menu [flags] [items...]
```

A single-selection list with a message area and a button row. Items come from arguments or stdin. Type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to accept.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Menu | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Text shown above the list |
| `--selected` | str | — | Item to place the cursor on |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Number of visible rows (0 = fit content) |
| `--cursor` | str | >  | Prefix drawn before the focused row |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='A custom button using print: emits its own value instead.'
| `↑/↓` | Move the cursor |
| `Enter` | Accept the focused item |
| `Tab` | Focus the buttons |
| `type` | Filter items |
| `Esc` | Clear the filter, or cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Clear the filter, or cancel'
zui menu --title "Restart" --message "Which service?" api web worker
printf 'small\nmedium\nlarge' | zui menu --title "Size"
zui menu --button "Open=accept" --button "Copy=print:copied" --button "Cancel=cancel" one two
```

**Notes**

line='zui menu --button "Open=accept" --button "Copy=print:copied" --button "Cancel=cancel" one two'
- A custom accept button prints the focused item. print: and run: actions behave as in msgbox.

## `checklist`

Mark any number of items and confirm with a button.

```text
zui checklist [flags] [items...]
```

A multi-select list. Space toggles the focused item; Enter activates the default button (usually OK). The accepted selection is printed one item per line.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Checklist | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Text shown above the list |
| `--selected` | multi | — | Items checked when the dialog opens (repeatable) |
| `--limit` | int | 0 | Maximum number of checked items (0 = unlimited) |
| `--no-limit` | flag | — | Allow any number of checked items |
| `--ordered` | flag | — | Return items in the order they were checked |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Number of visible rows (0 = fit content) |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='A custom accept button prints the focused item. print: and run: actions behave as in msgbox.'
| `↑/↓` | Move the cursor |
| `Space` | Check or uncheck the focused item |
| `Enter` | Confirm |
| `Tab` | Focus the buttons |
| `type` | Filter items |
| `Esc` | Clear the filter, or cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Clear the filter, or cancel'
selected=$(zui checklist --title "Features" ui docs tests)
printf 'a\nb\nc' | zui checklist --limit 2 --ordered
zui checklist --selected ui --selected docs --title "Keep" ui docs tests
```

**Notes**

line='zui checklist --selected ui --selected docs --title "Keep" ui docs tests'
- With no items marked, OK accepts the focused item.
- --ordered prints in selection order; otherwise list order is used.

## `form`

Fill several labelled fields, then confirm with a button.

```text
zui form --field 'Label=value' [--field ...] [flags]
```

A compact form dialog. Tab and Shift-Tab move between fields; Enter activates the default button. Each field is declared as Label=initial and values are printed one per line in field order.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Form | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Text shown above the fields |
| `--field` | multi | — | Field in Label=initial form; repeat for more fields (repeatable) |
| `--secret` | multi | — | Label of a field whose value is masked (repeatable) |
| `--button` | multi | — | Button in Label=action form (repeatable) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close with exit 124 after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--default-button` | int | 1 | Button triggered by Enter |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='--ordered prints in selection order; otherwise list order is used.'
| `Tab/Shift-Tab` | Next or previous field |
| `↑/↓` | Previous or next field |
| `Enter` | Confirm |
| `←/→` | Move the caret |
| `Esc` | Cancel |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Cancel'
zui form --title "New user" --field "Name=" --field "Email="
zui form --field "User=ada" --field "Password=" --secret Password --button "Create=accept" --button "Cancel=cancel"
zui form --field "Host=localhost" --field "Port=8080" --field Width=80
```

**Notes**

line='zui form --field "Host=localhost" --field "Port=8080" --field Width=80'
- Fields without an = are treated as labels with empty values.
- Values are printed in declaration order, one per line; use read or an array to capture them.

## `gauge`

Display a progress gauge, interactively or as plain output.

```text
zui gauge [flags]
```

Shows a filled bar with a percentage. By default it opens a dialog and waits for a key; --print (or a non-terminal stdout) writes the bar directly, which is handy in scripts.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--percent` | int | 0 | Percentage to display (0-100) |
| `--title` | str | Progress | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Label drawn under the bar |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close after a duration |
| `--print` | flag | — | Print the gauge to stdout instead of opening a dialog |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='Values are printed in declaration order, one per line; use read or an array to capture them.'
| `any key` | Close the dialog |
| `Esc` | Close the dialog |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Close the dialog'
zui gauge --percent 42 --message "Uploading"
zui gauge --print --percent 99 --width 30
for p in 0 25 50 75 100; do zui gauge --print --percent $p; done
```

**Notes**

line='for p in 0 25 50 75 100; do zui gauge --print --percent $p; done'
- The interactive gauge is static: pass a new percentage to show a new value.
- The bar assumes one cell per character.

## `infobox`

Show a message with no buttons; any key or a timeout dismisses it.

```text
zui infobox [flags] [message]
```

Useful for transient notifications. Esc never fails; the command exits 0 when dismissed and 124 when its timeout fires.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--title` | str | Info | Title shown in the title bar |
| `--message` | str | — | Body text (arguments are used when omitted) |
| `--icon` | str | info | Icon: info, success, warn, error, question |
| `--timeout` | str | — | Close automatically after a duration |
| `--width` | int | 0 | Dialog width in columns (0 = automatic) |
| `--height` | int | 0 | Dialog height in rows (0 = automatic) |
| `--border` | str | auto | Border: auto, rounded, sharp, double, thick, ascii, none |

**Keys**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
line='The bar assumes one cell per character.'
| `any key` | Dismiss |
| `Esc` | Dismiss |

**Examples**

```sh
line='Esc|Dismiss'
zui infobox "Deployment complete."
zui infobox --icon success --timeout 2s "All tests passed."
zui infobox --icon warn --title "Warning" "Certificate expires tomorrow."
```

**Notes**

line='zui infobox --icon warn --title "Warning" "Certificate expires tomorrow."'
- There are no buttons; use msgbox when the user must choose an action.
- A timeout returns 124, so scripts can distinguish automatic dismissal.

## `version`

Print version information.

```text
zui version
```

## `completion`

Generate a shell completion script.

```text
zui completion <zsh|bash>
```

Emit a completion script for zsh or bash. Load it from your shell configuration, e.g. eval "$(zui completion zsh)".

**Examples**

```sh
line='A timeout returns 124, so scripts can distinguish automatic dismissal.'
eval "$(zui completion zsh)"
zui completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/zui
```

**Notes**

line='zui completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/zui'
- The generated script completes command names and delegates file arguments to the shell. It intentionally does not complete every flag.
